subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Animal Farm, who is the farmer the animals overthrow in the Rebellion?
questions.explain: The animals rebel against the neglectful, drunken Mr Jones and drive him from the farm.

questions.q: Which two pigs become rivals for leadership after the Rebellion?
questions.explain: Napoleon and Snowball compete for control until Napoleon drives Snowball out.

questions.q: What does Squealer do to the Seven Commandments as the pigs break them?
options: He secretly alters them to excuse the pigs' behaviour
He carves new ones for the sheep
questions.explain: Squealer quietly rewrites commandments, such as adding "to excess" about drinking alcohol, to legitimise the pigs' conduct.

questions.q: Which Soviet leaders are Napoleon and Snowball generally taken to represent?
questions.explain: Napoleon represents Stalin and Snowball represents Trotsky, who was driven into exile.

questions.q: What does the cynical donkey Benjamin represent in the novella?
options: Weary scepticism and those who see corruption but do nothing
questions.explain: Benjamin distrusts the pigs and foresees disaster but stays passive, representing cynical inaction in the face of tyranny.

questions.q: Which character represents the Church through promises of "Sugarcandy Mountain"?
questions.explain: Moses the raven preaches of a paradise called Sugarcandy Mountain, satirising how religion can pacify the oppressed.

questions.q: In Animal Farm, the commandment 'All animals are equal' is finally altered to add which words?
options: 'but some are more equal than others'
questions.explain: The amended commandment exposes the pigs' hypocrisy and the betrayal of equality.

questions.q: Which pig acts as Napoleon's propagandist, persuading the animals to accept his decisions?
questions.explain: Squealer twists facts and rewrites events to justify Napoleon's rule.

questions.q: How does Napoleon finally seize sole power over the farm?
options: He sets his trained dogs on Snowball to chase him away
questions.explain: Napoleon unleashes the fierce dogs he reared in secret to expel Snowball.

questions.q: What ultimately happens to Boxer when he collapses from overwork?
options: He is sent to a peaceful retirement
He is sold to a knacker to be slaughtered
questions.explain: Napoleon sells the loyal Boxer to the knacker for money, despite claiming he was sent to a vet.

questions.q: What is Boxer the carthorse's personal motto?
questions.explain: Boxer's maxim "I will work harder" shows his loyalty and tireless effort.

questions.q: What simple slogan do the sheep bleat to summarise the Seven Commandments?
questions.explain: The sheep chant "Four legs good, two legs bad", a reductive slogan used to drown out dissent.

questions.q: What is the original final commandment, "All animals are equal", changed to?
options: "All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others"
questions.explain: The corrupted commandment exposes the pigs' hypocrisy and the betrayal of the revolution's ideals.

questions.q: Animal Farm is an allegory for which historical event?
questions.explain: Orwell's fable allegorises the Russian Revolution and the rise of Stalinist tyranny.

questions.q: Who does the pig Squealer represent as he spreads Napoleon's propaganda in Animal Farm?
questions.explain: Squealer is an allegory for Stalinist propaganda that manipulates the other animals.

questions.q: What does the windmill ultimately symbolise in Orwell's allegory?
options: The exploitation of workers' labour under a corrupt regime
questions.explain: The endlessly rebuilt windmill, which exhausts the animals while the pigs prosper, symbolises the manipulation and exploitation of labour.

questions.q: What major building project causes hardship and dispute among the animals?
questions.explain: The windmill, repeatedly built and destroyed, becomes a symbol of the animals' exploited labour.

questions.q: How does Napoleon justify taking the milk and apples only for the pigs?
options: Squealer claims the pigs need them as brainworkers to run the farm
The pigs won them in a vote
questions.explain: Squealer argues the pigs require the milk and apples for their brain-work, an early sign of their privilege and corruption.

questions.q: What is the novella's central message about power?
options: Animals make better leaders than humans
Power corrupts, and idealistic revolutions can be betrayed
questions.explain: Orwell shows how the pigs' growing corruption betrays the revolution, illustrating that power corrupts.

questions.q: Which old boar inspires the animals with a dream of rebellion before he dies?
questions.explain: Old Major's speech about freedom and the song "Beasts of England" sparks the revolution.

questions.q: In Animal Farm, what name do the animals give to the farm after the Rebellion?
questions.explain: The animals rename Manor Farm "Animal Farm" to mark their new self-rule, though the pigs later restore the old name.

questions.q: What happens to the windmill the first time the animals complete it?
options: It is destroyed in a storm, which Napoleon blames on Snowball
questions.explain: A storm topples the windmill, and Napoleon scapegoats the exiled Snowball to deflect blame.
